newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Visco says no new solidarity tax planned.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Visco says no new solidarity tax planned.

text.p: Italy's finance minister Vincenzo Visco denied on Wednesday in a newspaper interview that the government planned to introduce a new solidarity tax, and added government revenue in 1997 would be ahead of its forecasts.

Visco described the idea of a solidarity tax as a "strange idea" in an interview with the Rome-based La Repubblica newspaper, when asked if new taxes were necessary when Italy's Eurotax finishes later this year.
The Eurotax is being levied to make sure Italy reaches the key financial criteria for the single European currency.
He added that the higher value of the dollar was not of immediate concern, and there was no need for further measures to be added to the 1997 financial budget.
Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Sunday that this was the last summer Italy would have to be prepared to make sacrifices to help their country enter European Economic and Monetary Union.
